column1: # On-demand LoRA: adapters in the PVC, nothing declared in spec.model.lora.
# svc-d has NO spec.model.lora. attachLoRAAdapters returns early at
# len(adapters)==0 (workload_lora.go:148), so the controller injects neither
# --enable-lora nor a PVC mount. Both are supplied by hand in the fixture:
#   --enable-lora  via VLLM_ADDITIONAL_ARGS, which the preset interpolates into
#                  its `eval exec vllm serve ...` line
#   the PVC        via spec.template volumes/volumeMounts at /mnt/lora
# plus VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING=1 to register the mutation endpoints.
# manifests/fixture-ondemand.yaml
# --- what the workload starts with ---
property
controller-injected args
/v1/models at startup
openapi paths
adapters preloaded
# --- the route, which is the whole point ---
route
svc-a-kserve-route
svc-d-kserve-route
# 19 is exactly the 9A+19 floor at A=0. Loading three adapters at runtime left
# it at 19: on-demand loading spends ZERO match budget, permanently.
# --- reachability of adapters that are in NO route ---
# adapter-a3 loaded into svc-d at runtime; confirmed absent from svc-a and
# absent from every HTTPRoute in the namespace.
path
/lora-budget/svc-d/v1/chat/completions
/lora-budget/svc-d/v1/chat/completions
/lora-budget/svc-d/v1/chat/completions
/v1/chat/completions
/v1/chat/completions
/v1/chat/completions
/v1/chat/completions
# THE RESULT: the header only has to identify the POOL, not the adapter. One
# header entry - the base model, always present at A=0 - reaches every adapter
# that pool serves, because the BODY selects the adapter once the request
# arrives. The last row is the control: routing really did follow the header to
# a different pool, and that pool legitimately does not have adapter-a3.
# So the per-adapter matches are only needed when clients address an adapter BY
# NAME IN THE HEADER. Drop that requirement and the ceiling disappears with it,
# with flat adapter names intact and no controller change.
# CAVEAT, measured earlier in golden/authz-split.tsv: ODH's AuthPolicy rule
# deny-misrouted-model-header denies exactly this shape - header naming one
# model while the body names another. On ODH this pattern is refused by policy,
# not by the gateway. That rule would have to change for any of this to ship.
